page: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, alongside high throughput in software compilation and image processing. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 5123.16 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 192.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a Redis SET throughput of 120.37 million operations per second and a strong Passmark database score.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps but lacks local NVMe SSD storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data. While it lacks dedicated GPU hardware, its Intel AMX capabilities enable strong CPU-based LLM inference, processing 296.71 tokens per second on 7B models. The hardware profile offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, rendering it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for enterprise databases, large-scale caching layers, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, it includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The instance delivers top-tier performance in Geekbench multi-core testing and Redis SET operations, alongside strong memory read bandwidth of up to 192.43 GB/sec for large blocks. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. However, it lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on network-attached storage. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
